bottleneck: Producing clinical-grade viral vectors at scale is slow, variable, and expensive: cell-culture yields are low, purification must remove empty capsids and contaminants, and batch-to-batch consistency is hard to guarantee under GMP standards. For high-dose systemic therapies like SMA treatment, a single patient's dose can strain production capacity. Vector manufacturing, not biology, now gates many gene therapies, and capacity constraints create waiting lists for approved cures.
current_state: Suspension cell culture and improved purification are raising yields, but vector manufacturing remains a specialized, capacity-constrained industry with long lead times and few qualified facilities.

sources.title: Cell and gene therapy manufacturing: Challenges and Innovations in Scaling Up

title: Viral vector manufacturing cannot scale to demand
why_it_blocks: Even approved cures cannot reach patients if factories cannot make them. Manufacturing scarcity raises prices into the millions per dose and rations access to a privileged few, turning scientific victories into logistical failures.
